(a) Declaration of policy. It is the policy of the city that the proper operation of government requires that public officials be independent, impartial and responsible to the people; that governmental decisions and policy be made in proper channels of the government structure; that public office not be used for personal gain or harm to others; that the public have confidence in the integrity of its government and that public servants/officials are provided the information necessary to comply with these requirements. In recognition of these goals in this section and in the City Charter ethics requirements, this code of ethics and conduct for all persons serving or acting on behalf of the city as defined below (covered persons) is readopted with updates.
This section has the following purposes: (1) to encourage high ethical standards in conduct by covered persons in compliance with state Law, OCGA Sections 45-10-1, 45-10-3; (2) to establish standards of conduct for all such covered persons by setting forth those acts or actions that are expected of all such persons and those acts or actions that are incompatible with the best interest of the city; (3) to require disclosure by such covered persons of substantial private financial or other substantial interests in matters known to the covered person that affect the city; and (4) to serve as a basis for fairly and reasonably determining whether violations to this section have occurred and, if so, disciplining those who refuse to abide by its terms. The provisions of this Article shall not apply to political contributions, loans, expenditures, reports or regulation of political campaigns or the conduct of candidates in such campaigns.
(b) Scope of persons covered. This code of ethics and conduct supersedes all prior City of Madison ethics regulations (except the City Charter) and shall be applicable to: the Mayor and Council, Municipal Court Judge (prohibitions but not procedures in event of an alleged violation) and all City Officials as defined below (all the foregoing collectively referred to as "Covered Persons"). Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, state law and the Charter of the city shall be controlling in the event of an actual conflict with the provisions of this code of ethics and conduct. This section shall be interpreted to supplement, and not replace, said provisions of state law and the charter.
(c) Definitions. As used herein, the following terms shall have the following meanings, unless the context clearly indicates that a different meaning is intended:
(1) City official or covered person means the mayor, members of the council, city manager, assistant city managers, city clerk, deputy city clerks, municipal court judge, city attorney (whether such persons are salaried, hired or elected) and all other persons holding positions designated by the city charter, as it may be amended from time to time and all appointed officers, including all non-ad hoc officials, boards, authorities, commissions, and committees listed hereinbelow. Said list at this time includes without limitation (subject to future amendment) the following:
Planning commission, historic preservation commission (HPC), downtown development authority (DDA), audit committee, airport authority, bi-racial committee, business advisory committee, cemetery stewardship committee, corridor design commission, ethics committee, greenspace commission/tree board a/k/a greenspace conservation commission, Main Street advisory board.
(2) Confidential information means non-public intellectual property and/or information including engineering and technical designs and drawings, information (including ideas and concepts), services, processes, methods, technology, ideas, data, strategies, structure, design, architecture, goodwill, rates, pricing, financial information, business and/or marketing plans, projections, hypertext (HTML, CFM, and other), plans, graphics, documents, wording, documentation, user manuals, guides, instructional materials, layout and architecture, images, names, logos, or standards of or related to the city, and other similar information and intellectual property produced as ancillary and extensions thereof, except such information and intellectual property as the parties agree in writing is not proprietary or confidential and except information that has properly been made available to the general public including in open meeting or by appropriate authority.
(3) Entity means a sole proprietorship, partnership, limited partnership, firm, corporation, professional corporation, holding company, joint stock company, receivership, trust, LLC, LLP, LLLP or any other entity recognized by law through which business may be conducted.
(4) Decision means any ordinance, resolution, contract, franchise, formal action or other matter voted on by the city council or any non-ad hoc board, authority, commission, or committee listed in (c) 1) above, as well as the discussions or deliberations of such council, board, authority, committee or commission which can or may lead to a vote or formal action by that body.
(5) Discretionary authority means the power to exercise any judgment in a decision or action.
(6) Immediate family means spouse, mother, father, brother, sister, son, or daughter of any covered person related by blood, adoption, legal guardianship, or marriage. The relationship by marriage shall include in-laws.
(7) Remote interest means an interest of a person or entity, including a covered person, who would be affected in the same way as the general public. The interest of a covered person in property tax rate, general city fees, city utility charges, or a comprehensive zoning ordinance or similar decisions is incidental to the extent that the covered person would be affected in common with the general public.
(8) Incidental interest means an interest in a person, Entity or property which is not a substantial interest as defined below.
(9) Substantial interest means a known interest, either directly or through a member of the immediate family, in another person or entity: (1) the interest is ownership of $2,500.00 or more value of the voting stock, shares, market value or equity of the Entity; (2) funds received by the person from the other person or Entity either during the previous 12 months equaled or exceeded $2500; (3) the person serves as a salaried corporate officer or salaried member of the board of directors or other governing board of a for-profit entity wherein the person's salary is $2500 or more per year; or (4) the person is a creditor, debtor, or guarantor of the other person or entity in an amount of $2,500.00 or more. Substantial interest in real property means any interest in real property with said interest having a market value of $2,500.00 or more.
(10) Board or commission means any standing authority, board, commission, committee, entity, foundation, advisory group, or other similar body created by the city council or to whom the city council appoints members to represent the city.
(d) Prohibition of conflict of interest. A covered person may not participate in or be present for discussion of or a decision on a matter affecting a person, entity, or property in which said person has a substantial interest; in addition, a covered person who serves as a salaried corporate officer or member of the board of directors of a nonprofit entity, with salary of $2,500.00 or more per year, may not participate in or be present for discussion of or a vote or decision regarding funding by or through the city of said entity. Where the interest of a covered person in the subject matter of a decision is a remote or incidental interest, the person may participate in the decision and need not disclose the interest. At all times the covered person must uphold their oath of office, and support the City Charter, City Code and state and federal law.
(e) Standards of conduct. When serving or acting in an official capacity for the city:
(1) No covered person shall knowingly use such position to secure special privileges or exemptions for such person or others, or to secure confidential information for any purpose other than official responsibilities.
(2) No covered person, in any matter before a council, board or commission, in which he/she knowingly has a substantial interest, shall fail to disclose for the common good for the record such interest prior to any decision by the board, commission on which the covered person serves.
(3) No covered person shall act as an agent or attorney for another in any matter before the council or any board or commission with which the covered person is affiliated in any manner that would give rise to a conflict of interest as defined hereunder or under the City Charter or State law, including without limitation engaging in deliberation of the council or any board or commission with which the covered person is affiliated or the ex parte discussion of the client's matter with a member of the council or any board or commission with which the covered person is affiliated. It is permissible for the covered person to act only in a limited role, as an agent or attorney for another in a matter before the council or any board or commission with which the covered person is affiliated, for the limited purposes of providing factual information and raw data (not argument or advocacy) at the meeting and directly responding to questions from the council, board or commission. The preference is for such presentation to be primarily in written form. If questions are asked which elicit a verbal response, the covered person can present opinions and conclusions as long as all sides of the issue are fairly presented. Upon conclusion of the presentation and responses to questions, the covered person shall then recuse them self by leaving the room during the decision.
(4) No covered person shall directly or indirectly receive, or agree to receive, any compensation, gift, reward, or gratuity in any matter or proceeding connected with, or related to, the duties of his office except as may be provided by law. This is not intended to preclude the covered person from receiving lunch or dinner or gifts, such as Christmas, holiday or birthday gifts, which are a normal part of their non-official life with family, friends, and business relationships.
(5) No covered person shall enter into any contract with the city except as specifically authorized by law. Any covered person who has a substantial interest in either: an entity doing business with the city or which may wish to do business with the city in the future, shall make known that interest in writing to the mayor and council via the city clerk who shall inform, as appropriate, the board or commission.
(i) This prohibition and requirement shall not be applicable to an otherwise valid relationship between the city and a city official who is not elected (such as, by way of example, a city manager, city administrator, city judge, city attorney or chief of police).
(ii) Any official who has a substantial interest in an entity doing business with the city shall make that interest known in writing to the city council and the city clerk.
(iii) If this written disclosure is made, the city, under its standard purchasing procedures, may procure goods or services from an entity in which a covered person has a substantial interest without the covered person having to make additional disclosures.
(6) All public funds shall be used for the general welfare of the people and not for personal economic gain.
(7) Public property shall be disposed of per Georgia law.
(8) No covered person shall solicit or accept other employment to be performed or compensation to be received while still a covered person, if the employment or compensation could reasonably and objectively be expected to materially impair in judgment or performance of city duties.
(9) If a covered person accepts or is soliciting a promise of future employment from any person or entity who has a substantial interest in a person, entity or property which would be affected by any decision upon which said covered person might reasonably be expected to act, investigate, advise, or make a recommendation, said covered person shall disclose the fact to the board or commission on which he serves or to his supervisor and shall not participate in any action on matters regarding the potential future employer.
(10) No covered person shall use city facilities, personnel, equipment or supplies for private purposes, except to the extent such are lawfully available to the public.
(11) No covered person shall grant or make available to any person any consideration, treatment, advantage or favor beyond that which it is the general practice to grant or make available to the public at large.
(12) No covered person shall disclose any confidential information concerning any person, potential actions, property or governmental affairs of the city, without prior written formal authorization of the mayor and city council, board or commission, or his or her supervisor.
(13) No covered person shall use or permit the use of confidential information to advance the financial or personal interest of themselves or any other person or entity.
(14) No covered person shall appoint or vote for the appointment of any immediate family to fill an office, position, employment or duty when the salary, wages, pay or compensation is to be paid out of public funds.
(15) A covered person shall not use their position in any way to coerce, or give the appearance of coercing, another person to provide any financial benefit to anyone within the covered person's immediate family, or anyone with whom the covered person has business or financial ties amounting to a substantial interest.
(16) A covered person shall not order any goods and services for the city, board or commission without prior official authorization for such expenditure. No city official shall attempt to obligate the city nor give the impression of obligating the city without proper prior authorization.
(17) No covered person shall draw travel funds or per diem from the city for attendance at meetings, seminars, training or other educational events or other official functions and fail to attend such events without promptly reimbursing the city therefor.
(18) No covered person shall attempt to influence the outcome of a case before the municipal court of the city except in open court nor engage in ex parte communication with a municipal court judge on any matter pending before the municipal court.
(f) Disclosure.
(1) Any covered person who becomes aware that they have any substantial interest in any contract or matter before or within such entity or within any department of the city shall at the first practical opportunity disclose such private interest in writing to the city clerk and to the governing body of such agency or entity verbally at a public meeting thereof or in writing and such disclosure shall be entered on the records of said body and the covered person shall disqualify them self from participating in any decision or vote relating thereto.
(2) If the covered person participated in any decision or vote relating thereto, then thereafter realizes they may have had a substantial interest in the contract or matter, then said person shall disclose such private interest in writing to the city clerk and to the governing body of such agency or entity verbally at a public meeting thereof or in writing and such disclosure shall be entered on the records of said body. The matter shall be referred to the ethics committee. If it is determined that they had a substantial interest in the contract or matter, that individual's vote or decision shall be negated retroactive to the date of decision.
(g) Malfeasance, resources. Any covered person who knowingly conceals a substantial financial interest or knowingly in bad faith violates any of the requirements of this section shall be guilty of malfeasance in office or position and shall be punished as set forth below in section 2-1(n). To assist covered persons in meeting their responsibilities under this section, the city provides covered persons with a copy of this section and OCGA § 45-10-1 and OCGA § 45-10-3 and provides them with training and reasonable access to the city attorney, to guide them in the ethical and proper conduct of their meetings and official responsibilities.
(h) Exemptions. This code shall not be construed to require the filing of any information relating to any person's connection with, or interest in, any professional society or any charitable, religious, social, fraternal, educational, recreational, public service, civil or political organization, or any similar organization not conducted as a business enterprise or governmental agency, and which is not engaged in the ownership or conduct of a business enterprise or governmental agency.
(i) Severability. The provisions of this section are severable. If any provision of this section or the application thereof to any person or circumstance is held invalid, such invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of this section which can be given effect without the invalid provisions or application.
(j) Ethics committee.
(1) The mayor and council shall appoint an ethics committee consisting of one person, the city municipal court judge, to serve without compensation. The judge, in his discretion, shall be entitled to ask the city court solicitor to assist him in the investigation of complaints. Said judge shall be an attorney in good standing with the State Bar of Georgia and 21 or older, and resident of and/or practicing law in the City of Madison and registered to vote in Morgan County, and shall serve a three-year term. No person shall serve who is physically or mentally unable to discharge the duties of a member. If the judge is unable to serve due to conflict of interest or other cause, the mayor and council shall approve an alternative municipal court judge from another community.
(2) The member of the ethics committee must be approved by at least a four-fifths vote of the mayor and council.
(3) The position of the member shall be deemed vacated:
a. Upon the expiration of his or her term;
b. Upon the death of a member or the disability or incapacity of a member for more than 30 days;
c. Upon the written resignation of the member;
d. By the member ceasing to be a resident of Morgan County or a member of the Georgia Bar; or
e. Upon removal of the member for good cause by a majority vote of the mayor and council.
(4) The ethics committee member shall be prohibited from engaging in city election political activities and from making campaign contributions to candidates in city elections while a committee member. Violations of this subsection may be punished by removal by a majority vote of the mayor and council.
(5) The ethics committee member shall recuse them self if said member has a substantial interest, personal involvement, immediate family relationship, political relationship (e.g., political contribution, campaign involvement), or other conflict of interest with the Covered Person or matter being investigated. When the Ethics Committee Member recuses them self, the Mayor and Council shall appoint a qualified alternate member to hear the matter.
(6) If the ethics complaint is against the municipal court judge, the Georgia Judicial Qualifications Commission shall act as the ethics committee.
(k) Receipt of complaints and complaint process.
(1) All complaints shall be verified under oath in front of a notary public, and filed in writing with the city clerk and referred to the ethics committee. All written complaints shall contain a clear and concise statement of acts upon which the complaint is based along with an allegation that such facts constitute one or more violations of law, a reference to the statutory provision(s) allegedly violated, any further information which might support the allegations in the complaint including, but not limited to, name and address of all other persons who have first hand knowledge of the facts alleged in the complaint and any documentary evidence that supports the facts alleged in the complaint.
(2) The ethics committee may require that complaints illegibly or informally drawn be reduced to a complaint in proper form. The ethics committee shall in such instance advise the complainant of the defect in the complaint and that the complaint will not be considered unless the defect is corrected.
(3) Preliminary investigation. Upon receipt of a complaint, the ethics committee shall send a copy of the complaint to the accused affording an opportunity to respond to the complaint within seven days in writing, if desired. Responses or other documents submitted by the complainant or the accused after the seven-day period may be disregarded during the preliminary investigation.
(4) Preliminary investigation procedure. Upon receipt of a complaint in proper form and notice to the accused and the passage of more than seven days, the ethics committee shall, within two weeks of receipt of the original complaint, follow the procedure below:
a. Review. Review it to determine whether the complaint is unjustified, frivolous, patently unfounded or fails to state facts sufficient to show there may be "probable cause" (as defined by law) to invoke the disciplinary action, or is to be considered for further investigation.
b. Dismissal. Be empowered to dismiss those complaints which are unjustified, frivolous, patently unfounded or which fail to state facts sufficient to show there may be "probable cause" (as defined by law) to invoke the disciplinary jurisdiction of the mayor and council; provided, however, that a rejection of such complaint by the ethics committee shall not deprive the complaining party of any action he or she might otherwise have at law or in equity against the accused.
c. Filing. Be empowered to collect evidence and information concerning any complaint and to add the findings and results of its investigations to the file containing such complaint.
d. Hearings. Be empowered to hold hearings after at least seven days prior notice of the date, time and place thereof, personally hand delivered to the alleged violator. It shall conduct the hearing in accordance with the procedures and regulations it establishes but, in all circumstances, the hearing shall include the taking of testimony and the cross-examination of witnesses. The accused and the complainant shall have the right to be represented by counsel, to hear and examine the evidence and witnesses and to present evidence and witnesses in opposition or in extenuation. The ethics committee shall be empowered to adopt forms for formal complaints, subpoenas, notices, and any other instruments under these rules.
e. Recommendations. Make recommendations to the mayor and council (unless it is a city employee subject to the supervision and control of the city manager, in which case the recommendation will go directly to the city manager for disposition reasonably consistent herewith to the full extent permitted by the personnel policy), or to the State of Georgia if the allegations being investigated are against the mayor or council, including to discontinue further investigation if the complaint is unfounded (without "probable cause" as defined by law), or to effect remediation, and/or to invoke disciplinary action as described hereinafter.
f. Timeliness. All recommendations by the ethics committee shall be made to the mayor and council (or manager as described above) within 30 days of receipt of the complaint.
(l) Service of ethics committee recommendation; hearings and disposition of complaints.
(1) The recommendation by the ethics committee shall be reduced to writing and served upon all parties in interest and to the city clerk and to the mayor and council (or manager as described above) within five days of reaching a recommendation. Service shall be by personal service.
(2) The mayor and council shall take action upon the recommendation of the ethics committee at the next regular meeting of mayor and council following receipt of the recommendation, by discussing the recommendation from the committee based on the evidence presented at the hearing, as summarized by the presiding officer of the committee. Notice thereof shall be personally served upon the complainant and the accused at least five days prior to the meeting of mayor and council.
(3) The mayor and council shall deliberate in public, and reach a majority decision by public vote.
(4) The decision of the mayor and council (or manager as described above) shall be tendered to the accused and to the complainant within five days after completion of the hearing.
(5) Failure to strictly comply with any of the time deadlines in this ordinance, if the ethics committee and the mayor and council have proceeded without unreasonable delay, shall not invalidate any otherwise valid complaint or in any way affect the power or jurisdiction of the ethics committee or the city council to act upon any complaint.
(m) Right to appeal.
(1) Any accused or complainant adversely affected by the mayor and council decision (or in the case of a city employee, the city manager's decision) may appeal by petitioning for judicial review of such decision as provided in this section. Such decisions shall be reviewable by the Superior Court of Morgan County upon notice in writing via a petition for certiorari granted within 30 days of receipt of notice of said decision. The grant of such petition shall act as a supersedeas, staying the enforcement of the decision being appealed from.
(2) Review by the superior court shall, pursuant to Georgia Law, be limited to an inquiry of whether there was any evidence which supported said decision.
(3) Provided, however, no good faith action of the mayor and council or city manager refusing or failing to take action pursuant to this code of ethics and conduct shall be reviewable by the superior court.
(n) Penalties. Any person found to have violated any provisions of this section may be subject to written and oral reprimand or public censure by the mayor and council and/or request for resignation by the mayor and council (or in the case of a city employee, the city manager would issue such reprimand or request, or take other disciplinary action up to and including termination as per the personnel policy).
(o) Indemnification. Within the parameters of O.C.G.A. § 51-1-20 (Liability of members, directors, trustees or officers of nonprofit hospitals or associations, nonprofit, charitable, or eleemosynary institutions or organizations, or local government entities), if any person who was or is a party to or is threatened to be made a party to any threatened, pending or completed action, suit or proceeding, whether civil, criminal, administrative or investigative, seeks indemnification from the city against attorney's fees, which fees are reasonable in amount and were reasonably incurred by such person in connection with such action, suit or proceeding by reason of the fact that such person is or was a covered person and was acting in good faith within the scope of his or her official actions and duties, regardless of whether nature of person's actions at issue were ministerial or discretionary, and unless the damage or injury was caused by the willful or wanton misconduct of such person, then, unless such indemnification is ordered by a court, the city shall determine, or cause to be determined, in the specific manner provided under Georgia law whether indemnification is proper under the circumstances because the person claiming such indemnification has met the applicable standards of conduct set forth in the Georgia Code including without limitation OCGA § 45-10-3, and in the City Charter and the City Code of Ordinances. To the extent it is so determined that such indemnification is proper, the person claiming such indemnification shall be indemnified to the extent now or hereafter permitted by Georgia law. Attorney fee reasonableness shall be by the "lodestar" method approved by the Georgia Supreme Court or such other method approved by said court. The indemnification provided above shall not be deemed exclusive of any other rights to which those seeking indemnification may be entitled under the City Charter, ordinances and/or bylaws, or any agreement, or any vote of mayor and council or other disinterested body of which the covered person is not a member, or otherwise, as to action in the person's official capacity. To the extent permitted by Georgia law, the city may purchase and maintain insurance on behalf of covered persons.
(p) Downtown development authority specific provisions.
(1) The provisions of paragraph (9) of O.C.G.A. § 45-10-3 and of paragraph (1) of [OCGA § 36-62A-1(a)] shall be deemed to have been complied with and any such authority may purchase from, sell to, borrow from, loan to, contract with, or otherwise deal with any director or member or any organization or person with which any director or member of said authority is in any way interested or involved, provided (1) that any interest or involvement by such director or member is disclosed in advance to the directors or members of the authority and is recorded in the minutes of the authority, (2) that any interest or involvement by such director with a value in excess of $200.00 per calendar quarter is published by the authority one time in the legal organ in which notices of sheriffs' sales are published in each county affected by such interest, at least 30 days in advance of consummating such transaction, (3) that no director having a substantial interest or involvement may be present at that portion of an authority meeting during which discussion of any matter is conducted involving any such organization or person, and (4) that no director having a substantial interest or involvement may participate in any decision of the authority relating to any matter involving such organization or person. As used in this subsection, a "substantial interest or involvement" means any interest or involvement which reasonably may be expected to result in a direct financial benefit to such director or member as determined by the authority, which determination shall be final and not subject to review.
(2) Nothing contained in subsection (p)(1) of this Code section or in O.C.G.A. § 45-10-3 shall be deemed to prohibit any director who is present at any decision of the authority from providing legal services in connection with any of the undertakings of the authority or from being paid for such services.

Section 1150 Disclosure of Campaign Contributions and/or Gifts.
When any applicant for any zoning action, or any supporter or opponent of any zoning action who has contacted the City to express an opinion or who wishes to speak at a public hearing or submit written opinion, has made within two (2) years immediately preceding the filing of that application campaign contributions totaling two hundred and fifty dollars ($250.00) or more to an official of the City of Madison or to a member of the Planning Commission, it shall be the duty of said person to file a disclosure report with the City. In the case of the applicant, filing shall be within ten (10) days after the application is made, and in the case of a supporter or opponent, filing shall be at least five (5) days before the first public hearing. Such disclosure report shall include the name and official position of the official to whom the campaign contribution and/or gift was made, and the dollar amount, date, and description of each campaign contribution and/or gift made during the two (2) years immediately preceding the filing of the application.
Section 1160 Conflict of Interest In Zoning Decisions.
Any City Official who has a property interest in any real property affected by a zoning action which the City will consider, or has a financial interest in any business entity which has a property interest in any real property affected by a zoning action which the City will consider, or has a member of the family having any such interest, shall immediately disclose the nature and extent of such interest, in writing, to the Council. Such City Official shall disqualify himself from attending, participating in or voting on the zoning action. Disclosures made in accordance with this Section shall be public record and available for public inspection during normal business hours. Terms used herein are defined below.
(1) BUSINESS INTEREST: Any corporation, partnership, limited liability company, limited partnership, limited liability partnership, firm, enterprise, franchise, association, or trust.
(2) FINANCIAL INTEREST: All direct ownership interests of total assets or capital stock of a business entity of ten percent (10%) or more.
(3) CITY OFFICIAL. The Mayor, Council member, or any member of the Planning Commission.
(4) MEMBER OF THE FAMILY. The spouse, parent, sibling, or child of a City Official.
(5) PROPERTY INTEREST: The direct ownership of real property, including any percentage of ownership.

Charges for search, retrieval and production of copies is at the rate of the lowest paid full-time employee able to respond [O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(c)(1)], the first 15 minutes are free. The city charges for the cost of redacting records by a full-time employee [O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(c)(1)]. Fees for copying records are $0.10/page for letter or legal size documents. For odd-size printed documents, the actual cost of producing the documents is charged. For electronic records, the city charges the actual cost of the media on which the records or data are produced. [O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(c)(2)].
The city charges for requested records, even if not picked up [O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(c)(3)]. If estimated cost of producing records is over $500.00, the city requires prepayment before the search, retrieval, review or production of records [O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(d)]. If costs are not paid to the city for prior requests, it requires prepayment for all new requests, regardless of amount, until the previous charges are paid [O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(d)].

(a) Robert's rules. Except as otherwise provided in this section, the most recent edition of Robert's Rules of Order, Newly Revised, shall generally govern the conduct of council meetings.
(b) Call to order. Unless an executive session is approved, all meetings of the city council shall be open to the public. The mayor, or in his absence the mayor pro tempore, shall take the chair at the hour appointed for any regular, temporarily adjourned, special or called meeting, and shall immediately call the city council to order.
(c) Roll call. Before proceeding with the business of the city council, the city clerk or his deputy may call the roll of the members; and the names of those present shall be entered in the minutes.
(d) Quorum. A majority of all the members elected to the city council shall constitute a quorum at any regular or special meeting of the city council, and an affirmative vote of a majority of such number shall be sufficient to permit the conduct of all business except that for which a larger vote has been mandated by this Code.
(e) Orders of business. Unless otherwise decided by a vote of the mayor and council, the business of the council shall be taken up for consideration and disposition in the order set forth under section 2-43, "agenda."
(f) Reading of minutes. Unless a reading of the minutes of a city council meeting is requested by a member of the city council, such minutes may be approved without a reading if the city clerk has previously furnished each member with a copy of the minutes.
(g) Reports by committees.
(1) Any business coming before the city council concerning the subject matter of which any standing or special committee has jurisdiction may be referred to the proper committee for investigation and report. It shall be the duty of each standing or special committee, whenever required by the mayor or by the city council or any member of the city council, to examine any matter referred to such committee and make a prompt report or show good cause why no report is made. Such reports shall not be in writing unless so directed by the presiding officer.
(2) Each standing committee shall examine into the condition of the matters within its jurisdiction and make such reports and recommendations as may be necessary.
(h) Manner of addressing council. No speaker, while the city council is in session, shall speak on any subject unless recognized by the presiding officer. Every speaker shall address the chair, and no one shall interrupt anyone who is speaking except to call him to order or for explanation.
(i) Limitations on addressing council. Any person not a member of the city council who desires to address the council shall first secure the permission of the presiding officer to do so, and then shall step up in front of the council table, give his name and address in an audible tone of voice for the record, and direct his remarks to the city council as a body rather than to any particular member, limiting such remarks to ten minutes unless additional time is granted by the city council. The council is willing to receive written comment in lieu of a personal appearance and verbal statement at the council meeting, upon certain conditions. First, any written submission must be received by the mayor and council no later than 3:00 p.m. on the date of the scheduled meeting. Secondly, the written comment must be properly authenticated: for example, written comments should be signed and dated by the author, and should also provide the author's home address and telephone number. If the comment is received via email, there must be sufficient independent verification of the identity of the author to insure reliability of the communication. Third, the specific agenda item to which the comment relates must be clearly delineated in the body of the written communication. Fourth, the written communication should be succinct, clear, and non-repetitive in nature. In other words, the main theme of the author's comments should be stated once, and not repeated within the body of the written message. Fifth, the comment should be directed towards the council, not to the citizenry at large or persons other then the mayor and council. Sixth, the comment should be appropriate speech, free of inflammatory rhetoric and inappropriate statements lacking civility.
(j) Recording vote. Whenever any member shall request it, the yeas and nays of the members present shall be recorded in the minutes on any questions taken.
(k) Questions of order. The presiding officer shall decide all questions of order, but any councilmember who is dissatisfied with the decision may appeal to the city council in the manner provided by Robert's Rules of Order, Newly Revised, for appealing from decisions of presiding officers.
(l) Executive session. When any meeting is closed to the public per Georgia Law, the specific reasons for such closure shall be entered upon the official minutes, the meeting shall not be closed to the public except by a majority vote of a quorum present for the meeting, the minutes shall reflect the names of the members present and the names of those voting for closure, and that part of the minutes shall be made available to the public as any other minutes. Where a meeting is devoted in part to matters within the exceptions provided by law, any portion of the meeting not subject to any such exception, privilege, or confidentiality shall be open to the public, and the minutes of such portions not subject to any such exception shall be taken, recorded, and open to public inspection as provided in Georgia Law. Executive session minutes must be kept, but are confidential unless reviewed by a court in chambers. The executive session minutes will specify each issue. discussed in executive session. If matters are discussed subject to the attorney-client privilege, the fact that an attorney-client discussion occurred and the subject shall be identified, but the substance of the discussion need not be recorded or identified in the minutes [O.C.G.A. § 50-14-1(e)(2)(C)]. If a non-exempt topic is brought up in executive session, the mayor must immediately rule the discussion out of order. If the non-exempt discussion continues, the mayor must adjourn the meeting. When any meeting is closed to the public, the mayor and council shall execute and file with the official minutes of the meeting a notarized affidavit stating under oath that the subject matter of the meeting or the closed portion thereof was devoted to matters within the exceptions provided by law and identifying the specific relevant exception.

There is created a body, corporate and politic, to be known as the City of Madison Airport Authority, which shall be deemed to be a political subdivision of the state and a public corporation by that name, style and title; and the authority may contract and be contracted with, sue and be sued, implead and be impleaded, complain and defend in all courts of law and equity; except that the authority or the trustee, acting under the trust indenture provided for in this division, shall in no event be liable for any torts committed by any of the officers, agents and employees of the authority. The authority shall have perpetual existence.
(Code 1991, § 16-102)
100:
The authority shall be composed of seven members, five of whom shall be appointed by the city council. The mayor and the chairman of the board of commissioners of the county shall be ex officio members of the authority. It shall be the duty of the city council to appoint the members of the authority. The authority shall be composed of five posts, to be designated as Post No. 1, Post No. 2, Post No. 3, Post No. 4, and Post No. 5. The initial members appointed to Post No. 1 and Post No. 2 shall be appointed for a term which shall expire December 31, 1972, and until their successors are appointed and qualified. The initial members appointed to Post No. 3, Post No. 4, and Post No. 5 shall be appointed for a term which shall expire December 31, 1974, and until their successors are appointed and qualified. Thereafter, successors to the initial members of the authority who are appointed by the city council of the city shall be appointed in the year in which such members' respective terms of office shall expire and shall take office on January 1 following their appointment and shall serve for a term of six years and until their successors are duly appointed and qualified.
(Code 1991, § 16-103)
101:
Without limiting the generality of any provisions of this division, the general purpose of the authority is declared to be that of acquiring, constructing, equipping, maintaining, improving and operating airports and landing fields for the use of aircraft, including any related buildings and the usual and convenient facilities appertaining to such undertakings and extensions and improvements of such facilities, acquiring the necessary property, both real and personal, and to lease or sell any or all of such facilities, including real property, and to do any and all things deemed by the authority necessary, convenient or desirable for and incident to the efficient and proper development and operation of such types of undertakings.
(Code 1991, § 16-127)
102:
The first regular meeting of each year shall be in January. The authority shall meet at such times as may be necessary to transact the business coming before it, but not less than quarterly. At its first meeting in January of each year, the authority shall elect one of its members as its chairman and another member as secretary-treasurer. Only one person shall hold the office of secretary-treasurer. These officers shall be elected for a term ending on December 31 of the year in which they were elected or until their successors are elected and qualified. Three members of the authority shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of all business coming before it. The members of the authority shall be compensated as determined by the city council of the city; however, it is expressly provided that they shall be reimbursed for all actual expenses incurred in the performance of their duties.
(Code 1991, § 16-104)
103:
In the event of a vacancy on the authority by reason of death, resignation or otherwise, the vacancy shall be filled by the city council of the city; and the person so appointed shall serve for the remainder of the unexpired term.
(Code 1991, § 16-105)
104:
The authority shall have powers to:
(1) Have a seal and alter it at pleasure.
(2) Acquire by purchase, lease or otherwise, and to hold, lease and dispose of real and personal property of every kind and character for its corporate purposes.
(3) Acquire in its own name by purchase, gift or otherwise, on such terms and conditions and in such manner as it may deem proper, real property or rights of easements in such property or franchise necessary or convenient for its corporate purposes, and to use such property so long as its corporate existence shall continue and to lease or make contract with respect to the use of or disposition of such property in any manner it deems to be the best advantage of the authority.
(4) Appoint, select and employ officers, agents and employees, including engineering, architectural and construction experts, fiscal agents and attorneys, and fix their respective compensations.
(5) Make contracts and leases, and to execute all instruments necessary or convenient, including contracts for construction of projects, or lease of projects, or contracts with respect to the use of projects, which it causes to be erected or acquired, and any and all persons and any and all political subdivisions, departments, institutions or agencies of the state are authorized to enter into contracts, leases or agreements with the authority upon such terms and for such purposes as they may deem advisable; the authority is further granted the authority to make contracts and leases, and to execute all instruments necessary or convenient, with the United States government, or any agency or department of the U.S. government, concerning the projects of the authority, subject to the rights and interests of the holder of any of the bonds or obligations authorized to be issued and, by the resolution or trust indenture of the authority authorizing the issuance of any of its bonds or obligations, as provided in section 2-168.
(6) Construct, erect, acquire, own, repair, remodel and maintain, and to extend, improve, equip, operate and manage projects, the cost of any such project to be paid, in whole or in part, from the proceeds of revenue bonds or other funds of the authority or from such proceeds or other funds, and any grant from the United States or any of its agencies or instrumentalities.
(7) Accept loans and grants, or to accept loans or grants of money or materials or property of any kind from the United States or any of its agencies or instrumentalities or political subdivisions, or from any other source, upon such terms and conditions as the United States, or such agency or instrumentality, or other source may impose.
(8) Accept loans and grants, or accept loans or grants of money or materials or property of any kind from the state or any of its agencies or instrumentalities or political subdivisions, or from any other source, upon such terms and conditions as the state or such agency or instrumentality or political subdivision, or any other source may impose.
(9) Borrow money for any of its corporate purposes, and execute evidence of and secure such indebtedness, and issue negotiable revenue bonds payable solely from funds pledged for that purpose, and provide for the payment of such bonds and for the rights of the bondholders.
(10) Exercise any power usually possessed by private corporations performing similar functions, which is not in conflict with the constitution and laws of the state.
(11) Along with the trustees acting under the trust indenture, sell, lease, grant, exchange or otherwise dispose of any surplus property, both real and personal, or interest in such property, not required in the normal operation of and usable in the furtherance of the purpose for which the authority was created, except as such right and power may be limited as provided in this article.
(12) Regulate traffic at the airport.
(13) Do all things necessary or convenient to carry out the powers especially given in this division.
(Code 1991, § 16-107)
105:

The principal and interest of such revenue bonds shall be payable solely from the special fund provided for such payment. The bonds of each issue shall be dated, shall bear interest at such rates as may be authorized by the authority, shall be payable semiannually, shall mature at such time or times not exceeding 30 years from their date or dates, shall be payable in such medium of payment as to both principal and interest as may be determined by the authority, and may be made redeemable before maturity at the option of the authority, at such price or prices and under such terms and conditions as may be fixed by the authority in the resolution providing for the issuance of the bonds. Laws, page 36) amending the law formerly known as the Revenue Certificate Law of 1937 (1937 Ga. Laws, page 761); and all procedures pertaining to such issuances and conditions shall be the same as those contained in the Revenue Bond Law.
(Code 1991, § 16-108)
106:
The authority shall determine the form of the bonds and the places of payment of principal to such bonds, and shall fix the denomination of the bonds and the places of payment of principal and interest, which may be at any bank or trust company within or outside of the state. The bonds may be issued in coupon or registered form, or both, as the authority may determine; and provision may be made for the registration of any coupon bond as to principal alone and also as to both the principal and interest.
(Code 1991, § 16-109)
107:
In case any officer whose signature shall appear on any bonds or whose facsimile signature shall appear on any coupon shall cease to be an officer before the delivery of such bonds, such signature shall nevertheless be valid and sufficient for all purposes the same as if he had remained in office until such delivery. All such bonds shall be signed by the chairman of the authority and attested by the secretary-treasurer of the authority, and the official seal of the authority shall be affixed to the bond. 108:
All revenue bonds issued under the provisions of this division shall have and are declared to have all the qualities and incidents of negotiable instruments under the negotiable instrument law of the state. (Code 1991, § 16-111)
109:
The authority may sell bonds in such manner and for such price as it may determine to be for the best interest of the authority; but no such sale shall be made at a price less than par as provided in the Revenue Bond Law, unless the Revenue Bond Law is amended to permit the sale of such bonds at less than par.
(Code 1991, § 16-112)
110:
The proceeds of bonds shall be used solely for the payment of the cost of the projects; and, unless otherwise provided in the resolution authorizing the issuance of the bonds or in the trust indenture, additional bonds may in like manner be issued to provide the amount of any deficit for the cost of the projects which, unless otherwise provided in the resolution authorizing the issuance of the bonds or in the trust indenture, shall be deemed to be of the same issue, and shall be entitled to payment from the same fund without preference or priority of the bonds first issued for the same purposes. (Code 1991, § 16-113)
111:
Prior to the preparation of definitive bonds, the authority may, under like restrictions, issue interim receipts, interim certificates or temporary bonds, with or without coupons exchangeable for definitive bonds upon the issuance of the latter.
(Code 1991, § 16-114)
112:
The authority may provide for the replacement of any bond which shall become mutilated or be destroyed or lost.
(Code 1991, § 16-115)
113:
Revenue bonds may be issued without any other proceedings or the happening of any other conditions or things than those proceedings, conditions or things which are specified or required by this division. In the discretion of the authority, revenue bonds of a single issue may be issued for the purpose of any particular project. Any resolution providing for the issuance of revenue bonds under the provisions of this division shall become effective immediately upon its passage and need not be published or posted, and any such resolution may be passed at any regular or special or adjourned meeting of the authority by a majority of the quorum as provided in this division.
(Code 1991, § 16-116)
114:
Revenue bonds issued under the provisions of this division shall not be deemed to constitute a debt of the city, but such bonds shall be payable solely from the fund provided for in this division; and the issuance of such revenue bonds shall not directly, indirectly or contingently obligate the city to levy or to pledge any form of taxation whatever or to make any appropriation for the payment; and all such bonds shall contain recitals on their face to cover substantially the provisions of this section.
(Code 1991, § 16-117)
115:
In the discretion of the authority, any issue of revenue bonds under this division may be secured by a trust indenture by and between the authority and a corporate trustee, which may be any trust company or bank having the powers of a trust company within or outside of the state. Such trust indenture may pledge or assign fees, tolls, revenues and earnings to be received by the authority, including the proceeds derived from the sale of any surplus property of the authority, both real and personal. Either the resolution providing for the issuance of revenue bonds or such trust indenture may contain such provisions for protecting and enforcing the rights and remedies of the bondholders as may be reasonable and proper and not in violation of law, including covenants setting forth the duties of the authority in relation to the acquisition of property; the construction of the project; the maintenance, operation, repair and insurance of the property; and custody, safeguarding and application of all moneys, including the proceeds derived from the sale of property of the authority, both real and personal, and may also provide that any project shall be constructed and paid for under the supervision and approval of consulting engineers or architects employed or designated by the authority and satisfactory to the original purchasers of the bonds, and may also require that the security given by contractors and by any depository of the proceeds of the bonds or revenues or other moneys be satisfactory to such purchasers, and may also contain provisions concerning the condition, if any, upon which additional revenue bonds may be issued. It shall be lawful for any bank or trust company incorporated under the laws of this state to act as such depository and to furnish such indemnifying bonds or pledge such securities as may be required by the authority. Such indenture may set forth the rights and individual right of action of bondholders as is customary in trust indentures securing bonds and debentures of corporations. In addition, such trust indenture may contain such other provisions as the authority may deem reasonable and proper for the security of the bondholders. All expenses incurred in carrying out such trust indenture may be treated as a part of the cost of maintenance, operation and repair of the project affected by such indenture.
(Code 1991, § 16-118)
116:
The authority shall, in the resolution providing for the issuance of revenue bonds or in trust indenture, provide for the payment of the proceeds of the sale of the bonds to any officer or person who or any agency, bank or trust company which shall act as trustees of such funds and shall hold and apply the same to the purposes of this division, subject to such regulations as this division and such resolutions or trust indentures may provide.
(Code 1991, § 16-119)
117:
The revenues, fees, tolls and earnings derived from any particular project, regardless of whether or not such fees, earnings and revenues were produced by a particular project for which bonds have been issued and any moneys derived from the sale of any properties, both real and personal, of the authority, unless otherwise pledged and allocated, may be pledged and allocated by the authority to the payment of the principal and interest on revenue bonds of the authority as the resolution authorizing the issuance of the bonds or in the trust instrument may provide; and such funds so pledged from whatever source received, which pledge may include funds received from one or more or all sources, shall be set aside at regular intervals, as may be provided in the resolution or trust indenture, into a sinking fund, which sinking fund shall be pledged to and charged with the payments of:
(1) The interest upon such revenue bonds as such interest shall fall due;
(2) The principal of the bonds as such principal shall fall due;
(3) The necessary charges of paying agents for paying interest and principal; and
(4) Any premium upon bonds retired by call or purchase.
The use and disposition of such sinking fund shall be subject to such regulations as may be provided in the resolution authorizing the issuance of the revenue bonds or in the trust indenture; but, except as may otherwise be provided in such resolution or trust indenture, such sinking fund shall be a fund for the benefit of all revenue bonds without distinction or priority of one over another. Subject to the provisions of the resolution authorizing the issuance of the bonds or in the trust indenture surplus moneys sinking fund may be applied to the purchase or redemption of bonds and any such bonds so purchased or redeemed shall forthwith be canceled and shall not again be issued.
(Code 1991, § 16-120)
118:
Any holder of revenue bonds issued under the provisions of this division or any of the coupons appertaining to such bonds; and the trustee under the trust indenture, if any, except to the extent the rights given in this division may be restricted by resolution passed before the issuance of the bonds or by the trust indenture, may, either at law or in equity, by suit, action, mandamus or other proceedings, protect and enforce any and all rights under the laws of the state or granted in this division or under such resolution or trust indenture, and may enforce and compel performance of all duties required by this division or by such resolution or trust indenture, to be performed by the authority, or any of its officers, including the fixing, charging and collecting of revenues, fees, tolls and other charges for the use of the facilities and services furnished.
(Code 1991, § 16-121)
119:
The authority is authorized to provide by resolution for the issue of revenue refunding bonds issued under the provisions of this division and then outstanding, together with accrued interest. The issuance of such revenue refunding bonds, the maturities and all other details, the rights of the holders, and the duties of the authority in respect to the bonds shall be governed by the provisions of this division insofar as may be applicable.
(Code 1991, § 16-122)
120:
Bonds of the authority shall be confirmed and validated in accordance with the procedures of the Revenue Bond Law. The petition for validation shall also make party defendant to such action any municipality, county, authority, subdivision or instrumentality of the state, or the United States government, or any department or agency of the United States government, if subject to being sued, which has contracted with the authority for the services and facilities of the project for which bonds are to be issued and sought to be validated; and such municipality, county, authority, subdivision or instrumentality shall be required to show cause, if any, why such contracts and their terms and conditions should not be inquired into by the court and the validity of the terms be determined and the contract or contracts adjudicated as security for the payment of any such bonds of the authority. The bonds when validated and the judgment of validation shall be final and conclusive with respect to such bonds, against the authority issuing the bonds and any municipality, county, authority, subdivision or instrumentality of the United States government if a party to the validation proceedings, contracting with the authority.
(Code 1991, § 16-123)
121:
Any action to protect or enforce any rights under the provisions of this division or any suit against the authority shall be brought in the superior court of the county; and any action pertaining to validation of any bonds issued under the provisions of this division shall likewise be brought in such court, which shall have original jurisdiction of such actions.
(Code 1991, § 16-124)
122:
While any of the bonds issued by the authority remain outstanding, the powers, duties or existence of the authority or of its officers, employees or agents shall not be diminished or impaired in any manner that will adversely affect the interest and rights of the holders of such bonds; and no other entity, department, agency or authority will be created which will compete with the authority to such an extent as to adversely affect the interest and right of the holders of such bonds and, upon the issuance of bonds under the provisions of this division, shall constitute a contract with the holders of such bonds.

All moneys received pursuant to the authority of this division, whether as proceeds from the sale of revenue bonds, as grants or other contributions, or as revenues, income, fees and earnings, shall be deemed to be trust funds to be held and applied solely as provided in this division.

The authority is authorized to prescribe and fix and collect rates, fees, tolls and charges, and to revise and collect such rates, fees, tolls and charges for the services, facilities or commodities furnished, including leases, concessions or subleases or its lands or facilities, and in anticipation of the collection of the revenues and income of such undertakings or projects.

125:
It shall be the duty of the authority to prescribe rules and regulations for the operation of projects constructed under the provisions of this division, including the basis on which airports and landing fields for the use of aircraft shall be furnished.

On runway 14, the traffic pattern shall be a left-hand traffic pattern. On runway 32, the traffic pattern shall be a right-hand traffic pattern. Traffic pattern markings shall be installed so as to delineate these traffic patterns.

This division being for the purpose of promoting the health, morals and general welfare of the citizens of the United States, of the state, or of the city shall be liberally construed to effect its purposes.

Through the use and power of eminent domain, the authority shall have the right, power, privilege and authority to condemn real property, rights-of-way or easements for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of this division; any such condemnation shall be conducted in accordance with the laws of this state.

In the event of the death, resignation or removal of any member, his successor shall be appointed by the mayor to serve for the unexpired period of the term for which such member had been appointed; however, all members shall continue in office until their successors shall have been appointed.

The chairman, vice-chairman and secretary shall perform such duties as are commonly associated with their respective titles. The officers of the committee shall be and constitute the executive committee of the whole committee, which executive committee shall exercise such powers of the committee between its regular meetings as may be authorized by the committee. The committee shall be further authorized to appoint and fix the membership and number of standing and temporary committees as it may find expedient for the performance of its duties.
(Code 1991, § 22-104)
142:

(a) Private sale; when authorized. All bonds shall be sold at public sale upon sealed proposals, except that bonds may be sold at private sale:
(1) Without any previous public offering if:
a. Constituting all or part of an authorized issue of $20,000.00 or less; or
b. Sold to any board, body, agency, commission, instrumentality, district, authority or political subdivision of any local unit, the state or the federal government; or
(2) If no legally acceptable bid is received at advertised public offering, such bonds or any of them may be sold within 30 days after the advertised date for public bidding; however, no bonds shall bear interest at any rate of interest which is higher than the rate or maximum rate specified in the notice of sale, or contain substantially different provisions from those specified in the notice.
Any purchaser of bonds at private sale, other than a public body, shall deposit a certified or cashier's or treasurer's check drawn upon a bank or trust company in an amount equal to five percent of the amount of bonds purchased; and such amount shall be applied as in the case of a deposit made at public sale. Any private sale of bonds as permitted under this division shall be made or confirmed by resolution of the mayor and city council adopted by not less than a two-thirds vote of the full membership, which resolution shall set forth the date, maturities, interest rate and price of the bonds and the name of the purchaser.
(b) Publication of notice of bond sale. A public sale of bonds shall be advertised at least once and at least seven days prior to the sale in a newspaper of general circulation in the city and in a publication carrying municipal bond notices and devoted primarily to financial news or the subject of state and municipal bonds and published in the state.
(c) Procedure for public sale of bonds.
(1) All bidders shall be required to deposit a certified or cashier's or treasurer's check drawn upon a bank or trust company, equal to not less than two percent of the bonds to secure the city in part from any loss resulting from the failure of the bidder to comply with the terms of his bid, or as liquidated damages for such failure.
(2) All bids for bonds shall be publicly opened and announced at the advertised time and place of sale. Such bids as comply with the terms of the notice of sale shall be considered, and any bid not complying with the terms of such notice may be rejected. All bids received may be rejected.
(3) Bonds of two or more issues may be sold on the basis of combined maturities, or the maturities of each issue offered for sale.
(4) Bonds may be offered for sale at a single rate of interest, or bidders may be requested to name a single rate of interest; but no proposal shall be considered which offers to pay less than the principal amount of bonds offered for sale or which names a rate of interest higher than the lowest rate of interest stated in any legally acceptable proposal. As between proposals naming the same lowest rate of interest, the proposal offering to accept the least amount of bonds shall be accepted; the bonds to be accepted shall be those first maturing; and as between such proposals, the proposal offering to pay the greatest premium bid for the bonds shall in no event exceed $1,000.00 for the principal amount of bonds offered for sale. In order to effect the foregoing, a sufficient number of the last maturing bonds shall be of the denomination $1,000.00 or less.
(5) Bonds may be offered for sale at different rates of interest of the same issue or different rates of interest for different issues, or parts of issues, or bidders may be requested to name any such rates of interest. No proposal shall be considered which offers to pay an amount less than the principal amount of bonds offered for sale or under which the total loan is made at an interest cost higher than the lowest net interest cost to the local unit under any legally acceptable proposal. Such net interest cost shall be computed in each instance by adding to the total principal amount of bonds bid for the total interest cost to maturity in accordance with such bid, and by deduction of the amount of premium bid, if any.

The municipal budget shall be introduced, approved, amended and adopted by ordinance passed by not less than a majority of the full membership of the city council. The procedure shall be as follows:
(1) Public hearing. The municipal budget shall not be adopted until a public hearing has been held on the budget and taxpayers and all persons having an interest in the budget shall have been given an opportunity to present objections. Such hearing shall be held not less than 21 days after the initial approval of the budget at the time and place specified in the advertisement of the budget, and may be adjourned from time to time until the hearing is closed.
(2) Amendments.
a. The city council may amend the budget during or after the public hearing, except that no proposed amendment shall be effective without such a hearing if it shall:
1. Add a new item of appropriation in an amount in excess of one percent of the total amount of appropriations as stated in the initially approved budget;
2. Increase or decrease any item of appropriation by more than ten percent; or
3. Increase the amount needed to be raised by taxes by more than five percent.
b. Notice of hearing on any amendment shall be advertised at least three days before the date set for the hearing. Any such amendment must be published in full in the same manner as an original publication and must be read in full at the hearing and before adoption.
(3) Adoption. The municipal budget shall be adopted not later than permitted by state law. Upon adoption, the budget shall constitute an appropriation for the purposes stated in the budget and an authorization of the amount to be raised by taxation for the purposes of the city.

Alcohol means ethyl alcohol, hydrated oxide of ethyl, or spirits of wine, from whatever source or by whatever process produced and includes all alcohol, distilled spirits, beer, malt beverage, wine or fortified wine.
Alcoholic beverage means and includes all alcohol, distilled spirits, beer, malt beverage, wine or fortified wine.
Art shop. City means the mayor and council, or alternatively, where the context demands such, the area in Madison.
Church means a building primarily used for public religious worship on a regular basis.
Distilled spirits means alcohol obtained by distillation or more than 24 percent alcohol including, but not limited to, all fortified wines.
Fortified wine means any alcohol more than 21 percent alcohol made from fruits, berries or grapes, by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. The term includes but is not limited to brandy.
Governing authority or city means the mayor and city council, provided, however, where the context demands such, city means the geographical area within incorporated Madison, Georgia.

Licensee in article II of this chapter means any person selling, at retail, any alcohol in unbroken packages not for consumption on the premises.

Any person licensed for the sale of alcoholic beverages by the State of Georgia who possesses a license by a local government in the State of Georgia authorizing such person to sell or dispense alcoholic beverages by the drink off licensed premises and in connection with an authorized catered function.
Malt beverage means any alcohol obtained by fermentation of barley, malt, hops or any other similar product, or any combination of such products in water, containing not more than six percent alcohol by volume, and including ale, porter, brown, stout, lager beer, small beer and strong beer. The term does not include sake, known as Japanese rice wine.
Manufacturer means any maker, producer, or bottler of an alcoholic beverage. The term "manufacturer" also means in the case of distilled spirits, any person engaged in distilling, rectifying, or blending any distilled spirits; in the case of malt beverage, any brewer.
